summary: This note is an excerpt from the Wikipedia article on professional wrestling covering three topics: intergender singles matches, referee stoppages for unsafe wrestlers, and specialty match types. It also explains 'turns', where a wrestler changes between face (good guy) and heel (villain) alignment. The examples given include Luna Vachon, Chyna, ODB, Eric Young, Chris Jericho, Shawn Michaels, Sami Zayn, Hulk Hogan and Vince McMahon.
one_line: Wikipedia excerpt on professional wrestling covering intergender matches, referee stoppages, specialty matches like ladder and battle royal, and face/heel turns.
key_facts: Intergender singles bouts were first fought on a national level in the 1990s, beginning with Luna Vachon, who faced men in ECW and WWF.
Chyna became the first female to hold a belt that was not exclusive to women when she won the Intercontinental Championship.
In TNA, ODB participates in singles intergender matches, which is a rare feat in WWE.
Eric Young held the Knockouts Tag Team Championship for a record 478 days before it was stripped by Brooke Hogan because Young was a male.
A referee may stop a match when they or the official ring physician decides a wrestler cannot safely continue.
At the Great American Bash in 2008, Chris Jericho was declared the winner against Shawn Michaels when Michaels could not defend himself due to excessive blood loss and impaired vision.
At NXT TakeOver: Rival in 2015, the referee stopped the match when Sami Zayn could not defend himself due to an injury sustained against Kevin Owens for the NXT Championship.
In the basic ladder match, wrestlers must climb a ladder to obtain a prize hoisted above the ring, and the ladder can be used as a weapon.
The traditional ladder match prize is a championship belt, though prizes can also be a document granting a future title shot or a cash prize.
In a battle royal, 20-30 wrestlers are in the ring at one time, and the objective is to throw an opponent over the top rope with both feet on the floor.
WWE's Royal Rumble begins with two wrestlers, with others entering at 90-second intervals (previously 2 minutes) until 30-40 wrestlers have entered.
A character may 'turn', altering their face/heel alignment, either abruptly or through a slow build-up, almost always with a markable change in behavior.
Hulk Hogan's turn to heel after being a top face for over a decade is cited as a defining point in his career.
Frequent face and heel switching lessens the effect of turns and may result in audience apathy.
Vince McMahon is described as having more heel and face turns than anyone in WWE history.
